summary: Strong Boston Connor draft. The lead, all six recaps, the awards, the transactions and the preview trace cleanly to the brief, and every voice item passes except one factual slip. The Patriot of the Week blurb says Stevenson's run "started a 45-point day". ESPN has New England's scoring open with Maye's 35-yard touchdown to Douglas, so that sentence is wrong and blocks approval.

"Benedict Arnold would've kept the Patriots defense." (lead); "they throw you out of Fenway" (recaps[2]); "like the Bruins borrowing a goalie from Montreal" (recaps[3]); "One Patriot in the lineup, so A-minus." (awards[0]); "Patriot of the Week" award. No invented facts.

"A Bills quarterback carrying a team in my power rankings. Disgusting." (rankings[4]); "Seventeen catches and you still lose to Buffalo. Figures." (awards[3]); "an NFL record per ESPN. Split lost anyway." (asides.awards)

Real lines such as Warren's 80-yard catch and 50-yard run, Doubs's 1 catch for 16 yards, and Mevis's 0 for 2 lead to "That's on Kingslayers, not Doubs. Start him again next week or I riot." and "A kicker who scores negative isn't unlucky. He's a double agent."

Sarcastic and confrontational throughout: "Explain that to me." (lead), "Ninth feels generous." (rankings[8]), "Check who's playing. It takes ten seconds." (recaps[1]). The self-deprecating beats are thin: "I hate how this happened." (recaps[3]) and "RIGGED." (rankings[6]). UC never takes a real shot, which is a taste note (N2), not a miss.
No winking or "just kidding." "It works. It still feels wrong." (recaps[3]) reads as grudging, not as admitting the Bruins line is silly. "Bold. Stupid, but bold." (rankings[5]) stays in character.
"Pathetic." "Justice." "Figures." "Wasted." "Not enough." "Negative points. From a kicker." Lint average sentence length passes.
"Root for both teams in a rivalry game and they throw you out of Fenway." cuts into the Dak Side/Micah recap. "In a 12-team league I'd rank them 13th." cuts into the Elo take.
Occasional and not overdone: "Second place with that quarterback? Whatever." (rankings[1]); "Losing to a team whose namesake went negative?" (recaps[6]); "Now who plays quarterback?" (transactions)
"Dumbest move of the year." "Tenth is a gift." "The ghost lost." "Revoke his lineup privileges." All read as opinion about real numbers.
Three outbursts in the whole issue: "RAIDERS" (lead.body[0]), "ZERO." (recaps[1]), "RIGGED." (rankings[6]).

Dry stat run ("Maye completed 26 of 34 passes for 374 yards and four touchdowns") then "So they started the touchdown and the defense that allowed it." Dry Rams recap then "He's a double agent." Dry Shough recap then "Somebody unplug this team."

Insults and slang ("ghost", "ripoff", "Hung 226.24", "Disgusting"). Profanity is sensibly left out rather than forced.
"Pathetic." (lead), "Unbelievable." (recaps[3]), "Disgusting." (rankings[4]), "Unforgivable." (recaps[0]). Each is used once, where it is comedically justified.

Fenway, Bruins/Montreal and Benedict Arnold each appear once, in a spot where they fit. The Boston lines don't dominate the issue.
Plain language throughout; no polished transitions or elaborate metaphors. "Elo doesn't care how loud you win. Neither do I."
"Dumbest move of the year." "Seventh ... RIGGED." "Tenth is a gift."
"Elo got this one right." next to the Elo order; "Without him, maybe the Raiders win and ThePeopleBeaters look smart."; "Beating J'Allen is worth five bucks by itself."

items.evidence: "That run started a 45-point day." (awards[4]) puts Stevenson's 5-yard run at the start of the 45-point day. ESPN has the scoring open with Maye's 35-yard touchdown to Pop Douglas, and Stevenson's run comes after the Raiders tied it.

Absurd takes are all framed as opinion about real facts: "Without him, maybe the Raiders win and ThePeopleBeaters look smart." "Benedict Arnold would've kept the Patriots defense." "Revoke his lineup privileges." "Best money they've spent all year." Quotes and reasons (McVay, ESPN injuries, Rousseau block) are all in the brief.

Stat-line sentences carry the facts straight: "Jared Goff threw three touchdowns and ran in another at Arizona (28.94)." "Smack missed from 43 and 47 and pushed an extra point wide left Sunday, per ESPN." "Cincinnati's on bye, so fine."
Three caps outbursts total. "Unbelievable.", "Pathetic." and "Justice." each appear once. No repeated short sentences, and the lint passed.
The issue as a whole reads as one blunt, biased, deadpan-then-chaotic Patriots fan: the Raiders-defense lead, the "ghost" and "double agent" bits, and the Bruins/Fenway/Benedict Arnold references.

notes.problem: The brief's NE 45, LV 17 ESPN recap says New England opened the scoring on a 35-yard TD pass from Maye to Douglas after a 79-yard drive. The Raiders then tied it on Bowers's 13-yard TD. Stevenson's 5-yard run followed that tie. It did not start the 45-point day. A real number is attached to the wrong event. Rule: facts.md, number attached to the right play.
notes.fix: Cut the sentence or restate it from the recap: Maye's 35-yard touchdown to Douglas opened the scoring, and Stevenson's 5-yard run put New England back ahead right after the Raiders tied it (the existing preceding sentence already says this). Don't use a new number unless it goes in `derived`.

notes.quote: Three Texans and Drake Maye carry the sponsor
notes.problem: The headline credits Maye, but the body never mentions him or his 39.46. The lead and the Maye standout cover it, but this recap's own story skips the sponsor's biggest scorer. "A Boston team leaning on Texans" also calls UC a Boston team, which the brief never says. It is harmless as a bit, but nothing in the draft sets it up.
notes.fix: Add one short sentence with Maye's 39.46 (a brief number), or trim the headline to the Texans. Optionally drop "Boston" from the Bruins line.

notes.problem: The guide wants occasional self-deprecation, with UC getting it too. Every UC mention is flattering or a complaint on UC's behalf ("RIGGED.", "UC by a mile.", "Beating J'Allen is worth five bucks"). UC did start Henderson (4.80) and Waddle (4.80) at flex and bench Hurts (13.00), which is a free jab.
notes.fix: Optionally give UC one small dig, for example in the preview line or the ranking take, using a brief number.
